title: Tensor and adjunction compatibility of canonical ringed-topos path comparisons
statement:
Let $W,X_1,X_2,Y$ be topoi presented by sites small in the universe of [def-weil-size-convention], with sheaves of commutative rings and morphisms of ringed topoi $f_i:W\to X_i$, $g_i:X_i\to Y$ for $i=1,2$ [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism]. Fix an isomorphism $g_1f_1\cong g_2f_2$ of ringed-topos morphisms, compatible with the structural ring maps. Use the ordinary unbounded derived categories of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category], the canonical derived pullback/direct-image adjunctions, and the tensor comparisons $t_h:Lh^*(K\otimes^L H)\xrightarrow{\sim}Lh^*K\otimes^L Lh^*H$ of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. Put $P_i=Lf_i^*Lg_i^*$ and $V_i=Rg_{i*}Rf_{i*}$, with the composite adjunction $P_i\dashv V_i$ and its counit $e_i$ [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]. Let $\theta:P_2\xrightarrow{\sim}P_1$ be the canonical comparison obtained from derived pullback composition and the specified ringed commutation isomorphism. Let $c:V_1\xrightarrow{\sim}V_2$ be the canonical comparison obtained from the direct-image composition isomorphisms of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] and the same commutation isomorphism. Define
$$d_{i,K,H}=t_{f_i,Lg_i^*K,Lg_i^*H}\circ Lf_i^*(t_{g_i,K,H}):P_i(K\otimes^L H)\longrightarrow P_iK\otimes^L P_iH.$$
Then for all $K,H\in D(Y)$,
$$d_{1,K,H}\circ\theta_{K\otimes^L H}=(\theta_K\otimes^L\theta_H)\circ d_{2,K,H}.$$
Moreover $c$ is the conjugate of $\theta$ [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate]. Explicitly, for all $Z\in D(W)$,
$$e_{2,Z}\circ P_2(c_Z)=e_{1,Z}\circ\theta_{V_1Z}:P_2V_1Z\longrightarrow Z.$$
No exactness of the underived module pullbacks is assumed.

proof.text: Put $h_i=g_i\circ f_i$, $Q_i=Lh_i^*$ and $S_i=Rh_{i*}$. Apply [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons] to each composable pair $(f_i,g_i)$ and to the specified ring-compatible 2-isomorphism between $h_1$ and $h_2$. This gives the canonical comparisons $a_i:Q_i\xrightarrow{\sim}P_i$, $\kappa_i:S_i\xrightarrow{\sim}V_i$, and the induced comparisons $s:Q_2\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_1$, $r:S_1\xrightarrow{\sim}S_2$. They have exactly the K-flat pullback and normalized direct-image meanings used in the statement. Unwinding the two paths therefore gives $\theta=a_1\circ s\circ a_2^{-1}$ and $c=\kappa_2\circ r\circ\kappa_1^{-1}$. Write $T_{i,K,H}:Q_i(K\otimes^LH)\to Q_iK\otimes^LQ_iH$ for the tensor comparison for $h_i$. The lemma applies to arbitrary structural ring maps and unbounded complexes; no exactness of the module pullbacks is needed.

proof.text:
The monoidality assertions of [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons] say
$$d_i\circ a_{i,K\otimes^LH}=(a_{i,K}\otimes^La_{i,H})\circ T_i,\qquad T_1\circ s_{K\otimes^LH}=(s_K\otimes^Ls_H)\circ T_2.$$
Suppressing the displayed $K,H$ subscripts on $d_i,T_i$, substitute these equalities into the expression for $\theta$ from step 1:
$$\begin{aligned}
d_1\circ\theta_{K\otimes^LH}
&=(a_{1,K}\otimes^La_{1,H})\circ T_1\circ s_{K\otimes^LH}\circ a_{2,K\otimes^LH}^{-1}\\
&=((a_{1,K}\circ s_K)\otimes^L(a_{1,H}\circ s_H))\circ T_2\circ a_{2,K\otimes^LH}^{-1}\\
&=((a_{1,K}\circ s_K)\otimes^L(a_{1,H}\circ s_H))\circ(a_{2,K}^{-1}\otimes^La_{2,H}^{-1})\circ d_2\\
&=(\theta_K\otimes^L\theta_H)\circ d_2.
\end{aligned}$$
The third line follows by composing the first displayed equality for $i=2$ with the inverses of $a_2$ and $a_{2,K}\otimes^La_{2,H}$. All other rearrangements are associativity and bifunctoriality of tensor. This proves the tensor identity with the given $d_i$.

source.place: Tags 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product), 0D6D (lemma-derived-pullback-composition); elementary substitution of the existing monoidal comparison identities

proof.text:
The adjunction compatibility in [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons] is for the canonical adjunction $Q_i\dashv S_i$ and the composite adjunction $P_i\dashv V_i$ of the statement. With the conjugation convention of [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate], its composition assertion gives $a_i^c=\kappa_i^{-1}:V_i\to S_i$. Its 2-isomorphism assertion gives $s^c=r:S_1\to S_2$. Conjugation reverses composition and takes inverses to inverses, by [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate]. Thus
$$\theta^c=(a_2^{-1})^c\circ s^c\circ a_1^c=\kappa_2\circ r\circ\kappa_1^{-1}=c.$$
The inverse on $\kappa_1$ and absence of an inverse on $\kappa_2$ follow from their actual types, so this identifies the specified direct-image comparison, including its normalization.

source.place: Tags 0D6E (lemma-derived-pushforward-composition), 07A6 (lemma-adjoint); adjunction normalization supplied by the existing general coherence lemma and contravariant composition of conjugates

proof.text:
Finally [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate] identifies conjugation with the mate for identity intervening functors, and [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] characterizes that mate by its transpose. Apply this to $\theta:P_2\to P_1$ and the composite adjunctions. The transpose of $c_Z=(\theta^c)_Z$ under $P_2\dashv V_2$ is, by that characterization, $e_{1,Z}\circ\theta_{V_1Z}$. By the definition of the adjunction transpose of a map $V_1Z\to V_2Z$, it is also $e_{2,Z}\circ P_2(c_Z)$. Equating the two descriptions yields
$$e_{2,Z}\circ P_2(c_Z)=e_{1,Z}\circ\theta_{V_1Z}:P_2V_1Z\longrightarrow Z,$$
as required.
